summary: Okta attribute normalization mismatch prevents new console role provisioning after department rename
description: Issue summary: After a recent HR-driven department rename (Growth -> Go-To-Market) users in the renamed department are not receiving their console roles when their Okta profile is re-provisioned. Impact: 18 employees report 'No roles assigned' on the internal console and cannot access internal dashboards and feature flags. This blocks a small number of support and infra tasks for the GTM org. Environment: Production; SCIM provisioner v2.3.1; Okta org: redwood-prod.okta.com. Expected behavior: When Okta department attribute changes and SCIM reprovisions the user, RBAC role mappings should be applied to the console account automatically. Observed behavior: SCIM create/update completes but resulting user in console has no group memberships mapped; audit log shows mismatch between Okta attribute value and our expected normalization rules.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Okta admin, change a user's 'department' attribute from 'Growth' to 'Go-To-Market'
2) Trigger SCIM provisioning push (Okta > SCIM > push) or wait for scheduled sync
3) Observe the user row in Console > Admin > Users; expected RBAC group membership is missing
4) Attempt login: user authenticates via SSO but Console shows 'No roles assigned' and denies access to protected routes

comments: Marina Lopez (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed this first thing after HR renamed the department. Several GTM hires are blocked from submitting deploy requests.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged; collected logs and asked for list of affected users. Escalating to Identity team.

Devon Patel (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally. SCIM mapping layer lowercases and strips punctuation, our RBAC rules expect legacy short name 'growth' which doesn't match 'go-to-market' after normalization. Hypothesis: mapping table needs alias entries or a normalization rule change.

SRE (Tom Reynolds) 2026-03-11: Confirmed no errors in token exchange; this looks strictly mapping/transform related. Added temporary feature flag to bypass strict-match check for department->role mapping in provisioning service.

Identity (Priya Menon) 2026-03-12: Ran one-time backfill script to map legacy 'growth' alias to 'go-to-market' for affected users as temporary mitigation. Will follow up with PR to extend alias table.
investigation_notes: SCIM provisioning logs show update events but role assignment pipeline returns empty group list when normalized department value != expected key
Normalization pipeline: lowercase -> remove punctuation -> collapse spaces. 'Go-To-Market' -> 'go-to-market' but RBAC rules use 'growth' (legacy) -> mismatch
Workaround applied: one-time backfill mapped 18 users to the correct role in Console DB; users regained access around 2026-03-12 09:20Z
Root cause: HR migration renamed dept without creating alias mapping in our identity normalization table; provisioning assumes canonical keys without consulting alias mapping service
Risk: Future renames will repeat unless we implement alias resolution or make role mapping resilient to normalized synonyms
resolution: TBD - temporary backfill applied to restore access. Engineering to land PR that adds alias mapping and a normalization-tolerant lookup in the SCIM provisioner (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/482). Post-deploy runbook to add aliases for any HR-driven department rename. Planned rollout: patch to provisioner in next maintenance window, followed by audit to ensure no additional users are affected.
